title: Prophet + XGBoost Ensemble with Price Recommendation
description:
Forecasts daily demand per product and store with a blend of Prophet and XGBoost, then recommends a price for the forecast horizon.

  • Prophet models trend, weekly and yearly seasonality plus temperature, holidays and the price ratio to the competitor.
  • XGBoost learns non-linear effects of calendar, weather and price features.
  • The blend weight comes from each model's error on a 28-day hold-out window.
  • A price search picks the most profitable price inside a corridor (minimum margin, maximum gap to the competitor, maximum change per update), caps sales at stock on hand and explains the decision in one line.
  • Optional adapters cache forecasts in Redis and read sales events from Apache Kafka.

The example trains on synthetic sales data, so it runs anywhere without accounts.
implementationSteps: Export daily sales per SKU and store with price, competitor price, temperature and holiday flag (the example generates this data in data.py).
Add calendar and price features (day of week, day of year, weekend, our price / competitor price).
Train Prophet with weekly and yearly seasonality and the external regressors, and XGBoost on the feature table.
Hold out the last 28 days, measure MAPE of both models and set the blend weight by inverse error; retrain both on all history.
Forecast the next days from planned prices and the weather forecast; take the prediction interval from Prophet.
Estimate price elasticity with a log-log regression on history.
Search a price grid inside the business-rule corridor, cap expected sales at stock on hand and pick the price with the highest expected profit.
Optionally cache forecasts in Redis (4-hour TTL) and trigger re-forecasts from Kafka sales events.
Backtest on your own data with several cut-off dates before using the prices in stores.
performance:
Targets (not measured in production):

  • 7-day MAPE below 20 % per SKU/store on a rolling backtest.
  • Forecasts and price decisions refreshed every 4 hours.
  • Training one SKU/store on two years of daily data takes a few seconds on one CPU core, so 10,000+ SKUs need parallel jobs.

On the synthetic data in the example, the ensemble beats a naive 28-day-mean forecast in the tests; real sales data is noisier.
userExperience: Store managers see, per product, the demand forecast with an 80 % interval, the recommended price, the allowed price range and a one-line reason such as "Raise price: forecast demand (365) exceeds stock (250)". Pricing rules (margin, competitor gap, maximum change) are parameters, so the business can change them without retraining.
